chunks: With this chain, from al-Hasan, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala', who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Whoever recites these two Surahs and keeps them constantly in mind during his obligatory and voluntary prayers, Allah will not withhold any of his needs from him, and no barrier will stand between him and Allah, and Allah will continue to look at him with mercy until the accounting of all people is finished.'

key_terms.نُصْبَ عَيْنِهِ: constantly in view / kept in mind

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for reciting Surah Infitar and Inshiqaq in prayer?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Thawab al-A'mal*, this hadith emphasizes the transformative power of internalizing Surah al-Infitar and Surah al-Inshiqaq, which vividly describe the cosmic upheaval of the Day of Judgment. By making these chapters the focal point of one's prayer, the believer secures divine favor, ensuring that no obstacle hinders their needs and that they remain under Allah's watchful gaze until the final accounting of humanity.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1.  Imam Ja’far Sadiq (a.s.), “One who recites Surah Infitar and  Surah  Inshiqaq  in  his  obligatory  and  recommended prayer, Allah will eliminate all the barriers to the fulfillment of  his desires. There would be nothing to stop him. Allah will look at him with mercy till accounting of deeds of all the people is done.”
